steps.speaker: Pylgia
steps.content: The ship probably won't hold out much longer...
This morning, a loud crash came from the lower decks. Pylgia determined that the ship's hull is giving way.
Eroded by fog and seawater, paint has peeled from the upper deck, revealing metal rusted beyond recognition. It's only a matter of time before the keel and waterproofing fail.
Frankly, it's a miracle the ship's held together this long, after everything it's been through.

steps.speaker: Pylgia
steps.content: I was looking through Sigmund's shipping manifest yesterday. It lists some spare submarine parts in the cargo hold below.

steps.speaker: Pylgia
steps.content: The fog isn't as bad in the lower decks. Maybe those parts are still usable. We could try fixing one of the lifeboats...
Honestly, you don't see the point of this.
Neither of you knows much about mechanics. Even if you did, how long would it take to assemble a submarine...?
And what then? With no fuel or destination, where would you even go? How long could a tiny lifeboat last in this fog anyway?
But you can't bring yourself to say no to Pylgia, who refuses to give up.
